maximum_pilot.reason: Evidence supports offline/shadow experiments only. Stability and temporal integrity take priority.

findings.title: Treat market probability conversion as a model component, not a trivial normalization
findings.observed: Goto, Takeishi and Yairi (2026) evaluate 90,014 football matches across five bookmakers and report that their odds-only OO-EPC conversion outperforms existing odds-only methods for the majority of bookmakers; their one-parameter favourite-longshot-bias GLM also outperforms multinomial and ordered logistic alternatives in their experiments.
findings.derived: ARGUS should benchmark its current no-vig transformation instead of assuming normalized inverse odds are unbiased market probabilities. Market anchoring remains useful, but the transformation layer itself requires calibration evidence.
findings.hypothesis: A better de-vig/favourite-longshot correction will improve market-prior Brier/log-loss and reduce false edge near longshots/draws.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Offline replay only: compare current conversion vs multiplicative, power, Shin and OO-EPC/FL-bias correction using identical frozen odds snapshots and chronological folds.
findings.required_evidence: >=20,000 settled 1X2 observations across multiple bookmakers/leagues when available; report Brier, log-loss, RPS, reliability by probability bucket and bookmaker.
findings.failure_condition: No out-of-sample proper-score improvement, unstable gain across bookmakers/leagues, or apparent gain caused by timestamp/closing-price leakage.
findings.rollback: Retain current conversion; challenger remains offline only.

findings.title: Point-in-time feature construction must be a hard invariant
findings.observed: Sallis, Georgoulas and Tsoulos (Computation, 24 Aug 2026) benchmark 225,474 matches with a strictly chronological split. Their rolling features, Elo state and imputation use only earlier matches; static full-period means are explicitly avoided because they leak future information.
findings.derived: ARGUS should verify not only train/test chronology but every fallback statistic, rolling average, rating state, enrichment and imputation at decision_time.
findings.hypothesis: A point-in-time audit will expose silent leakage or optimistic historical evaluation that ordinary split checks miss.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Report-only invariant checker: for sampled predictions reconstruct every decision-critical feature with source_event_time <= decision_time; inject deliberately leaked fixtures as positive controls.
findings.required_evidence: >=1,000 reconstructed predictions spanning PREMATCH and LIVE plus synthetic leakage tests with 100% expected detection.
findings.failure_condition: Checker cannot distinguish event_time, ingest_time and settlement_time, or produces material false positives.
findings.rollback: Keep checker diagnostic-only; no blocking gate until validated.

findings.title: Do not increase model complexity without new information
findings.observed: The 24 Aug 2026 benchmark compares six materially different classifiers on the same 225,474-match feature space. Their performance is nearly identical; with market inputs they match but do not improve bookmaker log-loss, Brier or RPS. The authors conclude the information set matters more than model capacity in this setup.
findings.derived: ARGUS should require evidence that a new model adds information or stable residual signal, not promote it because it is more sophisticated.
findings.hypothesis: Simple residual/challenger models against the market prior will be as useful as heavier architectures unless ARGUS adds genuinely new sequential/live information.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Offline champion/challenger comparison using identical frozen features and folds: logistic/additive baseline vs current complex challenger, evaluated on proper scores and risk-coverage rather than hit rate alone.
findings.required_evidence: >=3 chronological test windows and paired bootstrap confidence intervals; improvement must repeat in at least 2 windows without worsening calibration.
findings.failure_condition: Only accuracy improves while proper scoring/calibration does not, or gains vanish under chronological resampling.
findings.rollback: Keep existing champion and record challenger as non-promoted.

findings.title: Bound API savings by explicit staleness rather than aggressive caching
findings.observed: Current Redis cache-aside documentation recommends TTL-bounded staleness, explicit invalidation on writes and protection against cache stampedes; it frames TTL as an upper bound on how stale a value may be served.
findings.derived: ARGUS can reduce duplicate provider calls safely only when cache TTL is tied to football-state sensitivity: long for static metadata, shorter pre-match, very short or invalidated on material LIVE state changes.
findings.hypothesis: State-aware TTL plus single-flight request coalescing can cut provider calls materially without increasing stale actionable decisions.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Shadow instrumentation only: calculate hypothetical cache hits and avoided calls while still fetching authoritative data; log freshness delta and whether a material event would have been missed.
findings.required_evidence: >=7 match-days, >=10,000 provider-read opportunities, including goals/cards/status transitions.
findings.failure_condition: Any hypothetical cache policy would have served stale score/red-card/status to an actionable decision, or savings are negligible.
findings.rollback: No cache-policy change; retain current fetch behavior.

findings.title: Selective forecasting should learn hard-to-predict states, but transferability is unproven for football
findings.observed: Inácio et al. (2026) propose selective time-series forecasting that predicts empirical error percentile from structural characteristics and reports improved forecast accuracy as difficult samples are rejected across heterogeneous time-series datasets.
findings.derived: ARGUS abstention could eventually use learned difficulty independent of raw model confidence, which may help when confidence itself is miscalibrated.
findings.hypothesis: A difficulty score based on data freshness, model disagreement, market dispersion, horizon and state volatility can improve loss at fixed coverage.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Paper-only meta-model predicting next-fold error/difficulty; compare risk-coverage against existing confidence/edge abstention. No change to PRIME/VALUE thresholds.
findings.required_evidence: >=5,000 settled predictions clustered by match and >=3 chronological folds; evaluate transfer across leagues and PREMATCH/LIVE separately.
findings.failure_condition: Coverage collapses, difficulty score fails cross-league transfer, or no improvement over simple abstention baselines.
findings.rollback: Discard meta-model; preserve current abstention logic.

findings.title: Control Plane truth should correlate decision IDs across logs, metrics and traces
findings.observed: OpenTelemetry defines common semantic conventions across traces, metrics, logs and resources, while Prometheus recommends urgent/actionable symptom-based alerts and grouping/deduplication rather than paging on every underlying cause.
findings.derived: ARGUS should make a single decision trace reconstructable end-to-end and reserve critical status for symptoms that can invalidate operator trust or decisions.
findings.hypothesis: A normalized telemetry envelope will shorten failure diagnosis and reduce duplicate/noisy alerts without hiding real incidents.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Emit shadow telemetry with decision_id, match_id, phase, provider, event_time, ingest_time, decision_time, freshness_ms, model_version, data_quality_state, settlement_state and error_type; no alert-routing changes initially.
findings.required_evidence: >=14 days of parallel telemetry and replay of at least 5 known failure classes.
findings.failure_condition: High-cardinality costs, missing provenance, trace correlation gaps or a previously visible critical symptom becomes less visible.
findings.rollback: Disable shadow emitter only; production health semantics unchanged.

findings.title: Formal champion/challenger aliases are useful, but a new registry dependency is not yet justified
findings.observed: MLflow Model Registry supports immutable model versions plus mutable aliases such as champion and tags for lifecycle metadata.
findings.derived: The governance pattern is useful for ARGUS, but installing MLflow solely for aliases would add operational surface. ARGUS can first reproduce the minimal semantics in its existing ledger/config layer.
findings.hypothesis: Explicit champion/challenger/version metadata will reduce accidental model drift and improve rollback clarity.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Add documentation/schema only for champion_version, challenger_version, evaluation_window, promotion_gate and rollback_target; do not add MLflow dependency.
findings.required_evidence: Demonstrate two complete offline challenger cycles and one simulated rollback using existing infrastructure.
findings.failure_condition: Existing versioning already provides equivalent traceability or schema creates conflicting sources of truth.
findings.rollback: Remove proposed metadata schema; no runtime dependency added.

findings.title: Reject algorithm novelty as a promotion criterion
findings.observed: The latest large football benchmark finds six distinct classifiers converge under a common chronological protocol, while proper scoring rules do not beat the bookmaker once market information is included.
findings.derived: Adding deeper neural, recurrent or attention architectures to the same static inputs has no current evidence basis for ARGUS.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: None required until a genuinely new sequential/event information source or strong residual hypothesis exists.
findings.required_evidence: Future proposal must show incremental information and repeated walk-forward proper-score improvement.
findings.failure_condition: Not applicable; rejected for insufficient evidence.

explicit_non_actions: No research result is represented as deployed
